**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in COL4A3 (HGVS:c.XXXZ) —DISRUPTS→ COL4A3 (HGNC:2212); COL4A3 (HGNC:2212) —DECREASES→ Type IV collagen assembly and cross-linking (GO:0033156); Type IV collagen assembly and cross-linking (GO:0033156) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0002709); Loss-of-function variant in COL4A3 (HGVS:c.YYYZ) —DISRUPTS→ COL4A3 (HGNC:2212); COL4A3 (HGNC:2212) —DECREASES→ Type IV collagen assembly and cross-linking (GO:0033156); Type IV collagen assembly and cross-linking (GO:0033156) —LEADS_TO→ Alport syndrome (MONDO:0957811). Mutations in COL4A3 impair the assembly and cross-linking of Type IV collagen, a critical component of basement membranes. This disruption leads to skeletal abnormalities characteristic of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia and the renal and auditory defects of Alport syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in COL4A3 with a minor allele frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD for both heterozygous and homozygous individuals would falsify the claim that COL4A3 is the sole or primary causal gene for both diseases. _(variant: COL4A3)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of COL4A3 in basement membrane integrity could reveal therapeutic targets for both skeletal dysplasias and kidney diseases, potentially involving strategies to stabilize collagen or enhance its assembly.
